declared_proposition: Let E_n tend to L>0, a_n=E_n-L, A_+=limsup n max(a_n,0), A_-=limsup n max(-a_n,0), J_n=n(E_n-E_(n+1)), and S_n=(n+1)E_(n+1)-nE_n. If A_+ and A_- are finite, then limsup J_n<=A_++A_- and liminf S_n>=L-A_+-A_-. Thus A_++A_-<L gives an eventual positive lag margin. The coefficient one on each one-sided envelope is jointly optimal, including the critical boundary A_++A_-=L.
mathematical_argument: Since a_n-a_(n+1)<=max(a_n,0)+max(-a_(n+1),0), J_n is at most n a_n^+ + [n/(n+1)](n+1)a_(n+1)^-. Taking limsups gives A_++A_-. The exact identity S_n=E_(n+1)-J_n and E_(n+1)->L gives the lag bound. For arbitrary P,M>=0, set a_n=P/n at even n and a_n=-M/n at odd n. Then the one-sided envelopes are P,M, the even subsequence has J_n->P+M and S_n=L-P-M, and the odd subsequence has S_n=L+P+M. Hence no smaller universal coefficient on either side is valid. These are abstract sequences, not Guinand-Weil packet energies.

finite_computation_boundary: Three abstract Fraction families and 192 rows are checked; none is an actual Weil packet.
logical_limit: The abstract criterion is now sharper, but neither one-sided reciprocal envelope is bounded for actual Guinand-Weil packets.
